News 
 
• Post lab 1 
Posted by Hasan Shodiev 
 
Edited 
Post lab Question (PQ) for lab #1:  
Estimate the Olympic swimming pool problem: 
 
An Olympic swimming pool is roughly 50.01m long and 31.45m wide. 
 
How long will it take to fill such a pool with an ordinary garden hose? 
 Hint: 
You need to make a reasonable estimate for the depth of the pool as you did in the lab for 
the IAs height and explain how you came up with the estimate.  Estimate the flow rate for 
the garden hose in the same way. Do the necessary calculations and explain your result.   
Postlabs: Post lab Question (PQ) and IQ4 and IT4 are due by one week. 
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
This post lab submission is due by one week at midnight after the lab session: 
i.e. if your upcoming lab is on Thursday, October 14 at 2:30pm; your post lab must be 
submitted by Thursday, October 21 at midnight. 
You should submit an electronic version of the post-lab question through the Dropbox of 
MyLS, Lab1 folder.  
LATE SUBMISSION: 
Deduction for late submission: 
----> One day late submission results in a 20% deduction. For example, you are 1 day late 
and get a score of 80 out of 100. After deducting 20% your updated score is 64 out of 100.

The first lab will be: 
• An introduction to the PC141 laboratory 
• Exercise 1: Estimation and Bounding 
This lab sets the foundation for experimental reasoning, approximation, and physical 
intuition that will be used throughout the course. 
 
Preparation for the First Lab 
Before attending your first lab session, please: 
• Read Chapter 1 of the PC141 Lab Manual

What to Bring to the First Lab 
Please bring: 
• A paper copy of Chapter 1 
• A lab notebook 
• A calculator 
Accurate record-keeping of experimental methods and data is an essential part of science. 
Your physics lab notebook should include: 
• Experimental procedures 
• Data and observations 
• Notes from pre-lab introductions 
• Sketches, estimates, assumptions, and reflections 
Your notebook is a scientific record, similar in spirit to historical laboratory notebooks (e.g., 
Alexander Graham Bell’s laboratory notes): 
 
 
Contact Information 
        Email: hshodiev@wlu.ca 
(Use your myLaurier webmail account only) 
Email guidelines: 
• Include your course and lab section in the subject line 
(e.g., PC141 – Lab Section L02) 
• Messages sent without course and lab section identification 
or outside MyLearningSpace may not receive a response
